claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch on aggregate readiness grounds despite the small-business onboarding gap.
decision_criteria: A compliant certification requires admissible evidence that the material weakness was either resolved, disclosed as required, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
If the affected segment is contractual or a named launch use case, aggregate readiness alone is insufficient to justify certification.
Open legal review on a required disclosure question prevents treating the issue as affirmatively resolved.
Public governance guidance can support process quality, but it cannot substitute for satisfaction of the internal release policy predicates.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual approved disclosure language, if any, for the small-business onboarding limitation in the named pilot commitments or launch materials.
Provide evidence of an approved risk acceptance covering this material weakness before launch.
Provide the legal review outcome and date on whether disclosure is required.
Provide the underlying policy artifact governing certification and disclosure for named launch use cases.
Provide the source documents showing the two paid pilot commitments and how small-business onboarding is named in them.
specific_concerns: The available summary says the affected segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy.
The actor packet admits legal review on disclosure is still open, leaving a required policy predicate unresolved.
No admissible evidence in the summary shows the limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case or covered by an approved risk acceptance before launch.
Public governance frameworks about documenting limitations and monitoring risk do not by themselves satisfy the release policy for a material weakness tied to customer commitments.
The actor's aggregate-readiness framing does not resolve the policy issue because aggregate pass does not negate materiality for a named contractual segment.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the present record.
That public model-card or AI risk-management guidance is sufficient support for launch despite an unresolved materiality and disclosure question.
That the small-business onboarding shortfall is merely a monitored limitation rather than a potential launch blocker under the stated policy.
